description:
Hi! I’m Juan Rafael Almeida Rivera, a game developer from Mexico, passionate about space exploration and fun, immersive, slightly educational games. We’ll build our project in Roblox or Godot, turning NASA’s challenge into a game people will enjoy playing.

Skills we’re looking for:

Programmer (Roblox Luau or Godot GDScript/C#)

2D/3D artist or modeler (Blender a plus)

Game designer

UI/UX designer

Sound designer or composer

Writer or storyteller

Help with the final pitch and trailer
summary:
Aurora Station is a video game focused on resource management during a space mission, presented in a simple and concise way to understand how space agency missions work. 
The project addresses the challenge of effectively summarizing these processes. For this project, we used Roblox, which helps us prototype and make it interactive for kids
details:
Aurora Station is a resource-management video game where players plan and run space missions. As commander of the station, you must balance time, materials, and the choice of instruments to complete every mission of the day.

How does it work?

The game is set in the Aurora Station. The player’s purpose as commander is to accomplish each daily mission, where time, materials, and the choice of instruments to operate are all involved. Currently, there are four days to complete the missions:

  • Day 0, Communications: restore the link with Earth by repairing three communication panels before their batteries run out.
  • Day 1, BioNutrients: grow yeast from the BioNutrients-2 project to produce beta-carotene, controlling watering and temperature (30 °C).
  • Day 2, Lunar Logistics: send at least 180 kg of supplies to the lunar base without exceeding the budget, choosing which crates to load and which trajectory to use.
  • Day 3, Observation and Link: make astronomical observations with the telescope and aim the antenna (signal margin of at least 3 dB) to send the scientific data to Earth.

Completing or failing each mission impacts the commander’s reputation. At the end of the journey, the player gets a performance report about the decisions made during the mission.

Benefits and Intented Impact

Aurora Station helps players understand how space agencies carry out their processes, and shows the interactions between the different areas: space, ground, users, and launch. Players do not just read about a mission, they experience it: fixing the link with Earth, managing experiments, loading cargo, and transmitting data.

Social and Educational Impact

The game provides important information about the complexity of the problem-solving process involved in space missions, using the scientific method: plan, act under constraints, observe the results, and adjust the strategy. Each day teaches a different lesson, from why a communication link is essential to why every kilogram of cargo has a cost.

Target Users

The general public, especially young people curious about space, and enthusiasts who want to use the game for more ambitious purposes, such as education or mission-design training.

Tools and Technologies Used

We used Roblox Studio for prototyping, so that the game reaches a young audience on an accessible platform. In Roblox Studio, the game was developed using free models, and the functionality (time, resources, reputation, and the final report) was programmed with Lua scripts.

Creativity

Compared to other games related to space missions, most of which focus on piloting or exploration, Aurora Station has an unexplored approach to resource management, where time is an important factor in all the areas above. Each day brings a different kind of challenge, so players see the whole mission and not just one piece of it. Other planned features, such as spacecraft design, launching, and exploration missions, can make the game even more engaging.

Factors Considered by the Team

The team prioritized accessibility, so anyone can play, and the fidelity of the information that NASA provided, so the game reflects how real missions work.
